name: Castello di Casole
positioning: Belmond's Castello di Casole, a Tuscan estate hotel that grew from a medieval castle, with a spa in a former wine cellar
best_for: Travelers who want a countryside Tuscan estate with a spa and a vineyard
Guests interested in castle history and country activities such as truffle hunting

facts.text: The history of the estate goes back to the Etruscans.
Condé Nast Traveler says the hotel was built on the ruins of a tenth-century castle.
Condé Nast Traveler describes the interiors as including terracotta tiles, exposed wood beams and a central courtyard with fountain.
Accommodation includes suites and signature villas.
The hotel has a panoramic infinity pool.
The hotel has a 24-hour fitness centre.
The estate has a vineyard and olive groves.
Emporio del Castello serves traditional Italian cuisine.

highlights.text: The Essere Spa is housed in a former wine cellar.
The heart of the hotel was once a medieval castle, built in 998.
Filmmaker Luchino Visconti's parties at the estate added Hollywood grandeur.
Country activities at the hotel include truffle hunting.

considerations.text: The hotel is a 1-hour drive from Florence Airport.
WhataHotel notes the remote countryside location requires transportation to nearby towns.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing reflects the exclusive castle experience.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Belmond Castello di Casole
